skill.name: azure-web-pubsub-ts
skill.description: Build TypeScript real-time messaging applications with Azure Web PubSub SDKs for server, client, and Express event-handler workflows.
skill.summary: TypeScript reference for Azure Web PubSub authentication, tokens, groups, clients, and Express handlers.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, TypeScript template literals, placeholder Azure endpoints, and documentation-only environment-variable examples. No prompt injection or malicious exfiltration intent was found. One medium semantic issue remains because the guide demonstrates logging a generated client access URL that can contain a bearer token.

remediation.issue: Generated client access token URL is logged in the example.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the logging example or replace it with a redacted status message. Warn users not to log access-token URLs.

remediation.issue: The access-key credential example can encourage hardcoded secrets.
remediation.suggestion: Present managed identity as the production default and state that access keys must come from a secret store.

semantic_findings.title: Access Token URL Logging Example
semantic_findings.description: The documentation prints a generated client access URL. Azure Web PubSub client URLs can contain bearer tokens, so this pattern can expose credentials in logs.

content.value_statement: Real-time messaging features need correct Azure Web PubSub setup across server and browser code. This skill provides TypeScript patterns for authentication, tokens, groups, clients, and Express handlers.
actual_capabilities: Shows package installation commands for Azure Web PubSub JavaScript SDKs.
Demonstrates service client authentication with connection strings, managed identity, and AzureKeyCredential.
Explains client access token generation with users, roles, groups, and expiration settings.
Provides server-side examples for broadcasts, user messages, group messages, and connection management.
Shows browser client setup, group joins, message sending, lifecycle handlers, and reconnect events.
Includes an Express event-handler pattern for connect validation, user events, and negotiation.
limitations: It is a documentation reference, not a runnable project scaffold.
It does not include automated tests or deployment configuration.
It assumes the user already has an Azure Web PubSub resource.
It does not cover every SDK option or advanced production architecture.

use_cases.title: Implement Secure Negotiation
use_cases.description: Use the Express handler and token examples to issue client access URLs after authentication.

use_cases.title: Review SDK Integration Choices
use_cases.description: Compare connection strings, managed identity, access keys, groups, and permissions before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Web PubSub Client

prompt_templates.title: Create a Negotiation Endpoint
prompt_templates.scenario: Backend endpoint for client access URLs.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design an Express negotiation endpoint that returns an Azure Web PubSub client access URL.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Group Messaging
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to outline TypeScript server and client changes for joining groups and sending group messages.

prompt_templates.title: Harden a Production Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review an Azure Web PubSub TypeScript integration for authentication, roles, groups, reconnection, and event handling.

output_examples.input: I need browser clients to receive live chat messages through Azure Web PubSub.
output: Recommended setup using WebPubSubClient with a negotiation endpoint.
Group join and send flow for chat-room messaging.
Lifecycle handlers to register before starting the client.

output_examples.input: I need a backend endpoint that issues Azure Web PubSub access URLs.
output: Express negotiation flow using the service client token API.
Guidance to attach authenticated user identity to the token.
Reminder to avoid logging generated access-token URLs.

output_examples.input: I want to compare authentication approaches for production.
output: Managed identity as the preferred production option.
Connection strings for local setup or controlled environments.
Access-key handling guidance for secret storage.

best_practices: Prefer managed identity with DefaultAzureCredential for production deployments.
Register client event handlers before starting the Web PubSub connection.
Validate users during connect handling before assigning groups or roles.
anti_patterns: Do not log generated client access URLs because they can contain bearer tokens.
Do not hardcode Azure access keys in application source code.
Do not grant broad group permissions when a user only needs one group.

faq.question: Does this skill create a complete application?
faq.answer: No. It provides TypeScript reference patterns for integrating Azure Web PubSub into an existing application.

faq.question: Which Azure SDK packages does it cover?
Can it help with browser WebSocket clients?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows WebPubSubClient setup, message sending, group handling, and connection lifecycle events.

faq.question: Can it help with server-side messaging?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows service client usage for broadcasts, users, connections, groups, permissions, and tokens.

faq.question: Does it include production security guidance?
faq.answer: It includes basic guidance, but users should add secret storage, token redaction, and authorization review.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
